zh.thesis: 左右两派关于托儿所影响儿童的说法都远超证据，实际影响可能很小。
paragraphs: 托儿所会不会伤孩子大脑？右翼评论员说会，左翼政客说它是万能药。极端说法两边都有，但证据都不足。
反对者举皮质醇为例，说孩子白天皮质醇升高是压力大。但皮质醇不是天生有害，正常波动很大，高也可能只是兴奋。
更离谱的是说托儿所让孩子大脑杏仁核早熟、萎缩，导致焦虑抑郁。这纯粹是猜测，没人做过这种研究。
支持者说托儿所带来高回报，比如奥巴马称每美元投入有七美元收益。但经典研究只针对极端弱势儿童，且样本小、方法旧，不能推广到全民。
随机试验也显示，托儿所的早期学业优势几年后消失，对社交能力影响好坏参半。唯一较肯定的好处是对弱势儿童。
所以托儿所效应既不是创伤也不是神药。与其吓唬焦虑的父母，不如让他们选最适合自己的方式。

en.thesis: Claims on both sides about daycare's effects far outstrip the evidence; real effects are probably small.
paragraphs: Does daycare harm children's brains? Right-wing commentators say yes, left-wing politicians call it a cure-all. Both extremes lack evidence.
Critics cite cortisol, saying kids' daytime rises signal stress. But cortisol isn't inherently bad, its levels fluctuate widely, and a rise could just mean excitement.
More outlandish is the claim that daycare causes the amygdala to mature early and burn out, leading to anxiety and depression. That is pure speculation; no such research exists.

Supporters tout big returns, like Obama's claim of seven dollars per dollar spent. But the classic studies involved only extremely disadvantaged kids, had small samples and dated methods, so generalizing is a stretch.
Randomized trials also show that early academic gains fade within years, and social effects are mixed. The clearest benefit is for disadvantaged children.
So daycare is neither trauma nor miracle. Better to let parents choose what works for them than to scare them.

articles.title: The Myth of Owning Your Time
articles.author: Nick Maggiulli

zh.thesis: 自己当老板并不会让你真正拥有时间自由，因为顾客、客户和股东会像老板一样占据你的时间。
paragraphs: 很多人以为自由职业或创业就意味着完全掌控自己的时间，想去哪就去哪，想什么时候工作就什么时候工作。但这通常只是一厢情愿。
一旦你为自己工作，你的日程同样会被塞满，只不过要求来自客户和供应商，而不是老板。你可能会在不合时宜的时候收到客户请求，员工也可能集体辞职，那时找替补的还是你。
而且越成功的人往往越忙。随着地位上升，每个人都想从你这里分得一点时间，说「不」变得异常困难。连 Kim Kardashian、Mark Zuckerberg 和 Jamie Dimon 都得随叫随到，回应赞助商、监管者或股东。
这并非从来如此。过去高收入者工作时间更短，但根据 NBER 的研究，从 1983 年到 2002 年，高收入人群长时间工作的比例反超了低收入人群。耶鲁教授 Daniel Markovits 也证实，如今最富有的 1% 比上世纪中叶多工作 4-5 小时，而底层 60% 则更少。
2018 年一项针对 27 位大公司 CEO 的研究显示，他们平均每周工作 62.5 小时，79% 的周末和 70% 的假期都在工作。你可能会说他们有权选择不工作，但从不使用的自由时间跟没有并无区别。时间不像金钱，无法转移或储存，一旦流逝就再也回不来了。
所以不必幻想一个你完全掌控每一分钟的理想世界。更好的做法是弄清楚你真正想在什么事情上花时间，然后为这些追求牺牲你的时间。生命中的一切有价值的东西都要求某种牺牲，而这是你选择的人生。

en.thesis: Going out on your own doesn't grant you real time freedom, because clients and shareholders occupy your hours just as a boss would.
paragraphs: Many people believe that freelancing or starting a business means total control over your time: work where you want, when you want. But that's usually wishful thinking.

Once you work for yourself, your schedule fills up just as much, only the demands come from customers and vendors instead of a boss. You'll field client requests at awkward hours, and when employees quit, you're the one who has to find replacements.

And the more successful you are, the busier you tend to be. As you rise, everyone wants a piece of you, and saying no becomes incredibly hard. Even Kim Kardashian, Mark Zuckerberg, and Jamie Dimon have to answer to sponsors, regulators, or shareholders when called upon.

It wasn't always like this. In the past, the wealthy worked fewer hours, but according to NBER research, by 2002 the top earners were twice as likely to work long hours as the bottom. Yale professor Daniel Markovits confirms that the top 1% now work 4-5 more hours than mid-century, while the bottom 60% work fewer.

A 2018 study of 27 large-company CEOs found they worked an average of 62.5 hours a week, including 79% of weekends and 70% of vacation days. You might say they had the freedom to choose otherwise, but never using your free time is the same as not having it. Time isn't like money; you can't save it or give it away—it just runs out.

So instead of dreaming of a world where you control every minute, figure out what you truly want to spend your time on, and then give it up for those pursuits. Everything valuable in life requires sacrifice, and this is a life you've chosen.

articles.title: Welcoming First-Year Students with a Wake-Up Call
articles.author: conversableeconomist

zh.thesis: 美国大学对新生说的欢迎辞从“你们是罪人”变成了“你们是最优秀的”，这种自满损害了学术赖以生存的谦卑与好奇。
paragraphs: 每年秋天，全美大学都宣称迎来了史上最优秀、最多样化的一届新生——这听起来就不可信。哥伦比亚大学教授安德鲁·德尔班科认为，这种自满是精英院校自找的，它们流露出的优越感让外界反感。
他回忆，早期东北部名校多为新教背景，校长会对新生说：“你们都是无用的罪人，全靠神的恩典才在此，你们不配。”而如今的话术变成了“欢迎来到我们伟大的大学，你们是最棒的”。
德尔班科认为，认真做学问离不开自我怀疑和好奇，而这种“我们已掌握答案”的傲慢恰恰扼杀了它们。所以，给新生的欢迎辞应当降调，多些谦卑。

en.thesis: American colleges' welcome speeches have shifted from “you are sinners” to “you are the best,” and that smugness undermines the humility and curiosity academic work depends on.
paragraphs: Every fall, colleges across the country claim they are welcoming the best, most diverse freshman class ever — which strains belief. Columbia professor Andrew Delbanco says such smugness is of the elite institutions' own making, and their sense of superiority is what turns people outside the gates against them.

He recalls that the early Northeastern colleges, mostly Protestant in origin, had presidents who told incoming students: “You are all worthless sinners. You're here by the grace of God; you have not earned it.” Today's version is “Welcome to our great university. You are the best and brightest to ever walk through the gate.”

Delbanco argues that serious scholarship requires self-doubt and curiosity, and the arrogance of “we have it figured out” kills both. So the message to freshmen should be moderated, and humility restored.

articles.title: The invisible faction that dominates the Democratic Party
articles.titleZh: 主宰民主党却看不见的派系：进步建制派
articles.author: Matthew Yglesias

zh.thesis: 民主党真正的支配力量不是激进的造反派，而是被忽视的进步建制派，他们通过基金会、捐赠者和非营利网络掌握着实际权力。
paragraphs: 关于民主党内部派系的议论，常被简化成「激进左派对抗温和建制」的框架。但作者认为，这过分简单，忽略了最重要的一股力量——进步建制派。他们既不同于桑德斯式的造反派，也不同于温和派。
进步建制派是什么人？他们支持奥巴马第二任期左转，2016年虽选希拉里却乐见桑德斯逼她左倾，2020年视沃伦为最佳选择。在众议院，进步核心小组有近一百名成员，他们不靠个人魅力，而是拥有庞大的基金会、捐赠者和非政府组织网络。
造反派则不同。他们像伯尼一样对党内体制充满敌意，愿意跳级挑战在任者，比如普拉特纳在缅因州挑战州长。而进步建制派的弗拉纳根，尽管更左，却绝不会在初选中挑战克拉布查尔，她就是个正常的普通民主党人。
两派有时合作，但本质不同。进步建制派更在乎具体的政策胜利，比如让领袖同意反对基石输油管；造反派则更看重自己人掌权。拜登政府里涌入大量沃伦派人员，却几乎没有桑德斯的亲信，就是这个区别的体现。
让温和派沮丧的是，造反派的戏剧性掩盖了进步建制派的主导地位。拜登的国内议程几乎全来自进步智库和倡导组织，没有克林顿式福利改革或奥巴马式绩效工资那样的温和举措。进步建制派确实做了组织工作，但结果不佳令人尴尬。
造反派的未来取决于桑德斯。如果他传给奥卡西奥-科尔特斯，她可能继承领导地位；否则运动可能分裂并被进步建制派吸收。作者认为那是遗憾，因为造反派敢于冒险、可能推动建设性变革，而进步建制派只会无止境地协调联盟利益。
所以，想让民主党更愿意对利益集团说「不」的人，应该把矛头指向进步建制派，而不是造反派。造反派领袖埃尔-赛义德在密歇根州民调落后，但这场运动了解成败的重要性。作者宁可看到自信的造反派，也不愿看到无尽的利益集团粘连。

en.thesis: The Democratic Party's true dominant force is not the radical insurgents but the overlooked Progressive Establishment, which wields real power through foundations, donors, and NGO networks.
paragraphs: Commentary on Democratic Party factions often flattens everything into a 'radical left vs. moderate establishment' frame. But the author argues this is too simplistic and overlooks the most important force: the Progressive Establishment, distinct from both Bernie-style insurgents and moderates.

Who are they? They supported Obama's second-term leftward pivot, backed Hillary in 2016 but were glad Bernie pushed her left, and saw Warren in 2020 as the best of both worlds. In the House, the Congressional Progressive Caucus has nearly 100 members, who rely not on charisma but on a vast network of foundations, donors, and grant-funded NGOs.

The insurgents are different. They are hostile to the party establishment, willing to jump the line, like Platner in Maine. In contrast, Flanagan, though further left, would never primary Klobuchar; she is a regular normie Democrat.

The two groups sometimes collaborate but differ in essence. The Progressive Establishment cares more about specific policy wins, like getting leaders to oppose the Keystone XL pipeline; the insurgents care more about taking over the party. The Biden administration was staffed with many Warrenites but few Sanders loyalists, reflecting this difference.

What frustrates moderates is that insurgent drama hides the Progressive Establishment's dominance. Biden's domestic agenda came almost entirely from progressive think tanks and advocacy groups, with no moderate or reformist initiatives like Clinton's welfare reform or Obama's performance pay. They did the organizing, but it didn't work well, which is embarrassing.

The insurgents' future depends on Bernie. If he passes the torch to AOC, she may lead; otherwise, the movement may fragment and be absorbed into the Progressive Establishment. The author would regret that, as insurgents take risks and could drive constructive change, unlike the endlessly coalition-managing establishment.

So those who want Democrats to say 'no' to interest groups should target the Progressive Establishment, not the insurgents. Insurgent leader El-Sayed is trailing in Michigan, but his movement knows the stakes. The author would rather have confident insurgents than an endless parade of interest group goo.

zh.thesis: 亚马逊的搜索广告是一种合法盗窃，最终由消费者买单。
paragraphs: 这不算税——税带来公共服务，这只是合法盗窃。亚马逊每周从搜索广告赚近十亿美元，足够给每位员工发三万五千美元奖金还有余。
作者的新书出版社也在亚马逊买搜索广告，每次点击约一美元。搜索「Seth Godin The Knot」时，你本来就要买这本书，却要付钱让广告先展示。
广告使搜索结果更差。最好的空气炸锅厂商为了保住原本的销售，也得买广告。而搜索广告是零和游戏：总销量不变，只是内部分配。
付费广告反而让电商售出更少商品。每年五百多亿广告费，最终由消费者承担——产品变贵，或新品开发被抽走精力。
这还带来两个副作用：厂商为省钱做劣质品来腾出点击预算；平台有动力让自然搜索结果变差，逼你买更多广告。亚马逊曾为消费者创造价值，如今却在偷他们的钱。

en.thesis: Amazon's search ads are legal theft, and customers end up paying.
paragraphs: It's not technically a tax—taxes fund public goods. This is simply legal theft. Amazon makes nearly a billion dollars a week from search ads, enough to give each employee a $35,000 bonus and still have change.

The author's publisher buys search ads on Amazon at about a dollar per click. Search for 'Seth Godin The Knot' and you'll see an ad for the very book you came to buy, and the publisher pays for that click.

The ads make search worse. The best air fryer maker has to buy ads too, just to keep the sales they'd have gotten anyway. And these ads are zero-sum: total category sales stay flat, merchants just fight over shares.

One study shows an ecommerce site with search ads sells fewer items than the same site without them. The $50 billion-plus spent annually on such ads is ultimately paid by customers—through higher prices or reduced innovation.

Two perverse effects follow: producers cut quality to fund click budgets, and platforms have incentive to degrade organic results to push more ads. Amazon once created value for customers; now it's stealing from them.

articles.title: Chinese carmakers now sell one EV abroad for every two at home
articles.titleZh: 中国车企现在每在国内卖两辆电动车，就往国外卖一辆
articles.author: Indranil Ghosh

zh.thesis: 中国电动车出口激增已从机会变成必需，且伴随而来的价格战将重塑海外市场。
paragraphs: 中国电动车企在国内失去买家，却在巴西、泰国和海湾地区找到了新市场。7 月，中国出口了 54 万辆电动车，创月度纪录，而国内销量约为 98 万辆，出口与国内之比从去年同期的 1:5 升至 1:2。
这种转向是长期的，而非对短期困境的反应。国内价格战已持续两年，如今正随汽车出海蔓延。分析人士指出，中国车价廉物美、技术先进，如同当年日本和德国汽车进军海外一样。
国内销量下滑与产能过剩是推手。2026 年前七个月，国内销量下降 12%，国际能源署预计今年市场将首次持平。正如咨询公司 Automobility 创始人所说：“我们已经从出口机会转向出口必需。”
下一个阶段是本地化制造和供应链。同时，库存积压迫使降价，过去 18 个月有超过 100 万辆电动车未售出，今年出口的仅三分之二找到买家。这意味着折扣和促销将持续，甚至特斯拉也在用出口弥补国内疲软。

en.thesis: Chinese EV exports have shifted from opportunity to necessity, and the accompanying price war is set to reshape overseas markets.
paragraphs: Chinese EV makers have lost buyers at home and found new ones in Brazil, Thailand, and the Gulf. In July, they exported 540,000 EVs, a monthly record, while selling about 980,000 at home — a ratio of one exported for every two sold, up from one in five a year earlier.

The shift is permanent, not a response to a bad year. The domestic price war, now two years old, is following the cars overseas. Observers say Chinese cars are cheap, widely available, and packed with tech, much like Japanese and German cars in their export heydays.

Falling sales at home and overcapacity are the drivers. Domestic sales dropped 12% in the first seven months of 2026, and the IEA expects the market to stay flat this year for the first time this decade. As one analyst put it: 'We've moved from export opportunity to export necessity.'

The next phase is localizing manufacturing and supply chains. Meanwhile, inventory glut forces price cuts: over a million EVs shipped in the last 18 months remain unsold, and only two-thirds of this year's exports have reached buyers. Expect discounts and incentives — even Tesla is leaning on exports to offset weak home sales.

articles.title: Morocco facts of the day, Morocco is not hopeless
articles.titleZh: 摩洛哥的今日事实：摩洛哥并非无望
articles.author: Tyler Cowen

zh.thesis: 摩洛哥已取代南非成为非洲工业化领头羊，正成为欧洲的出口基地。
paragraphs: 几十年来，南非一直是非洲工业化的成功典范，但去年摩洛哥超越它，成为非洲开发银行工业指数排名第一的经济体。
摩洛哥的成功靠的是地理位置和丰富的磷酸盐储量，它借此与美国、欧盟及五十多个国家签了自贸协定，目标是做欧洲的「工作台」，就像墨西哥之于美国。
它正转向电动汽车制造，与雷诺、Stellantis 合作，并在卡萨布兰卡建了非洲首家电池超级工厂，年产 70 吉瓦时，可满足欧洲当前市场三分之一的需求。
航空制造也是重点，空客、波音、泰雷兹、赛峰都来投资，航空出口十年翻三倍，接近 30 亿美元。此外，政府还批准了绿色氢能工业园，计划生产氨、钢铁和工业燃料，总值 325 亿美元。
所以摩洛哥不是靠运气，而是靠明确的产业政策和区位优势，把制造业一步步抓在手里。

en.thesis: Morocco has overtaken South Africa as Africa's leading industrial economy and is positioning itself as Europe's export-base workbench.
paragraphs: For decades South Africa was the great success story of African industrialization, but last year Morocco took the lead, ranking first on the African Development Bank's industrialization index.

Morocco's success rests on its location and its huge phosphate reserves, which it has leveraged into free-trade agreements with the US, the EU and fifty other countries. Its ambition is to be Europe's workbench, the way Mexico is for the US.

It is pivoting its car industry to electric vehicles, working with Renault and Stellantis, and has built Africa's first battery gigafactory in Casablanca. The 70-gigawatt-hour plant alone could supply a third of Europe's current market.

Aerospace is another focus, with Airbus, Boeing, Thales and Safran investing, and exports in that sector more than tripling over the decade to 2024, to nearly $3 billion. The government has also approved a green hydrogen industrial park set to produce ammonia, steel and industrial fuel worth $32.5 billion.
So Morocco's rise is not luck but a deliberate industrial policy, using its geography and resources to build manufacturing strength step by step.

articles.title: X's Algorithm Feeds Off Ragebait and Impacts Democrats More, Study Finds
articles.titleZh: 研究发现 X 的算法偏爱怒火，且对民主党影响更大
articles.author: Matthew Gault

zh.thesis: X 的算法为了互动量会不停推送让人生气的帖子，而民主党用户更容易陷入这个循环。
paragraphs: 一项发表在《美国国家科学院院刊》上的新研究发现，X 的算法会根据你讨厌什么，给你看更多同类内容。它优先考虑互动量，而不是你的真实偏好。
研究团队招募了 715 名美国用户，在 2024 年大选前安装浏览器插件，收集他们的信息流。还用一个价值观量表，测出每个人的核心价值观。
结果发现，点赞和转发会带来更多相似内容，但真正影响算法的是回复。回复只占互动的 6.8%，却能极大改变信息流走向。
算法学会了：你生气、回复，它就喂更多让你生气的帖子。这个恶性循环在民主党用户身上尤为明显，共和党用户则较少遇到。
X 前产品主管确认，算法确实曾把愤怒的回复当作重要信号，但上个月已调整，把朋友帖子的回复权重提高了 15 倍，怒火内容因此大幅减少。

en.thesis: X's algorithm learns what makes you angry and feeds you more of it, and Democratic users get caught in this loop more often.
paragraphs: A new study in PNAS found that X's algorithm learns what you hate and shows you more of it. It prioritizes engagement above everything else, not what you actually want to see.
The researchers recruited 715 American users before the 2024 election, installed a browser extension to collect their feeds, and measured their core values with a standard values inventory.
Likes and reposts brought more of the same, but the real driver was replies. Replying accounted for just 6.8% of interactions, yet it had an outsized effect on what the algorithm showed next.
The algorithm learned: you get angry, you reply, it feeds you more outrage. This loop was especially strong for Democrats, who saw more rage bait than Republicans.
X's former head of product confirmed that angry replies were once a key signal, but a month ago they boosted the weight of replies to friends by 15x, and rage bait dropped by an order of magnitude.

articles.title: Pornhub's Parent Company to Pay $120 Million to Settle Child Sexual Abuse Lawsuits
articles.titleZh: Pornhub 母公司以 1.2 亿美元和解儿童性虐待诉讼
articles.author: Samantha Cole

zh.thesis: Pornhub 母公司同意支付 1.2 亿美元，和解两起指控其平台传播儿童性虐待内容的集体诉讼。
paragraphs: Pornhub 的母公司 Aylo 将支付 1.2 亿美元，和解两起指控其平台违反联邦性交易和儿童性虐待图像法律的诉讼。这两起集体诉讼于 2021 年在加州和阿拉巴马州提起。
诉讼称，Mindgeek（现已更名为 Aylo）从施虐者上传到其平台的儿童性虐待内容中获利。其中一位原告说，她 16 岁时被前男友将性虐待视频传到 Pornhub 上。
和解涵盖了 2011 年至 2024 年间出现在 Mindgeek 旗下网站上的所有未成年人的视频和图像。Aylo 表示和解不承认任何责任，但同意加强内容审核，包括验证上传者年龄、人工和自动审查，以及向当局举报疑似虐待内容。
Aylo 称许多承诺已实施多年。此前 Pornhub 已因类似指控被 Visa 和 Mastercard 等支付机构封禁，并因此整改了安全措施。这一和解标志着这些争议的法律程序告一段落。

en.thesis: Pornhub's parent company will pay $120 million to settle lawsuits alleging its platforms profited from child sexual abuse material.
paragraphs: Aylo, the parent company of Pornhub, will pay $120 million to settle two class action lawsuits claiming its platforms violated federal sex trafficking and child sexual abuse imagery laws. The suits were filed in California and Alabama in 2021.

The plaintiffs alleged that Mindgeek, now Aylo, profited from child abuse material uploaded by abusers. One woman said her ex-boyfriend posted videos of her abuse when she was 16. Another said her trafficker uploaded videos and profited via Pornhub's Modelhub program.

The settlement covers anyone under 18 whose image appeared on Mindgeek sites between 2011 and 2024. Aylo denies wrongdoing but agreed to stricter moderation, including verifying uploaders' ages, human and automated review, and reporting suspected abuse to authorities.

Aylo says many of these measures were already in place. Previously, Pornhub had been dropped by Visa and Mastercard over similar allegations, leading to a trust and safety overhaul. This settlement marks another step in resolving those legal battles.

articles.title: The National Park Service Is Using Flock. Rangers Are Pissed
articles.titleZh: 国家公园管理局用上了 Flock 监控摄像头，护林员很恼火
articles.author: Joseph Cox

zh.thesis: 国家公园安装 Flock 车牌识别摄像头，侵犯了游客的隐私和自由。
paragraphs: 负责管理美国国家公园的国家公园管理局（NPS）在优胜美地等公园安装了 Flock 摄像头。现任和前任护林员对此很不满。一位现任护林员说：「Flock 保护的是财产，不是人或公园。人们应该自由地以尊重生态的方式休闲，但这种监控是对隐私的无礼侵犯。」
Flock 摄像头会持续扫描每辆过往车辆的车牌、颜色、型号等特征，生成带时间戳的记录，从而追踪车辆和人的位置。这些数据可供执法部门查询，通常无需搜查令。许多摄像头还接入全国网络，其他州的警察也能调用。
此前已有多起警察滥用 Flock 数据跟踪他人、甚至配合 ICE 的报道，引发了全国对 Flock 的讨论。护林员担心，如果游客知道自己的行踪被监控，会感到不安。
NPS 回应称，摄像头主要用于交通监测，不连接执法或 DMV 数据库。但护林员指出，去年优胜美地曾篡改规则，如果这种不当行为与跟踪能力结合，美国人将不再自由。他们害怕游客因车牌误读而被持枪拦下。

en.thesis: License plate surveillance in national parks violates visitors' privacy and freedom.
paragraphs: The National Park Service (NPS) has installed Flock cameras in parks including Yosemite. Current and former rangers are unhappy. One current ranger said, 'Flock protects property, not people or parks. People should be free to recreate respectfully, but this surveillance is a disrespectful invasion of privacy.'

Flock cameras constantly scan license plates, colors, models, and other features of every passing vehicle, creating timestamped records of where vehicles—and by extension people—were. This data is available to law enforcement, often queried without a warrant. Many cameras are part of a national network that other agencies can query.

There have been reports of police abusing Flock to stalk people and performing lookups for ICE, fueling a national debate. Rangers worry that visitors would be disturbed to know their movements are tracked.

NPS says the cameras are for traffic monitoring only and not connected to law enforcement databases. But rangers point out that Yosemite recently backdated a rule change, and if such malfeasance is combined with tracking, Americans are no longer free. They fear visitors being pulled over at gunpoint due to plate misreads.

articles.title: Screwworm Infections Get Worse, Government Unleashing Drone Army For Surveillance
articles.titleZh: 螺丝虫感染恶化，政府出动无人机大军监控
articles.author: Timothy Geigner

zh.thesis: 政府为应对螺丝虫疫情的花费已超过当初取消防治计划省下的钱，这是典型的捡了芝麻丢了西瓜。
paragraphs: 螺丝虫卷土重来，在得克萨斯州出现了几十年来首例。原本有个与拉美国家合作的防疫计划，但被 DOGE 削减经费砍掉了。
螺丝虫靠苍蝇在牲畜身上产卵，几周就能要了宿主的命。现在墨西哥有数百人感染，美国这边疫情也在恶化。
政府于是把边境巡逻的无人机调来查牲畜。至少 200 架无人机参与，已飞了 1226 架次，调查了 2.3 万头牲畜。
养不育蝇来灭虫也要花钱：墨西哥花了 2100 万，得州和亚利桑那的设施各花了千万级。被砍的防疫计划只值 1.7 亿，而现在疫情可能造成的损失高达 18 亿。
所以这笔账怎么算都不划算。省了小钱，赔了大钱，还搭上食品安全，这届政府的短视让人无语。

en.thesis: The government's response to the screwworm outbreak has already cost more than the program it cut, a textbook case of penny-wise, pound-foolish.
paragraphs: Screwworm is back, with the first case in Texas in decades. A prevention program run with Latin American countries was killed when DOGE cut its funding.
Screwworm flies lay eggs in livestock and can kill a host in weeks. Hundreds of people in Mexico are now infected, and the problem is worsening on the US side.
So the government has diverted border patrol drones to inspect cattle. At least 200 drones are involved, flying 1,226 missions and checking 23,000 animals.

Raising sterile flies to control the pest costs too: $21 million in Mexico, and tens of millions for facilities in Texas and Arizona. The canceled program was worth $170 million, while the outbreak could cause $1.8 billion in damage.
The math never works out. They saved small money, lost big money, and risked the food supply. It is a stunning failure of stewardship.

articles.title: Universal health coverage could save $1T and 114k lives a year: study
articles.titleZh: 研究称全民医保每年可省 1 万亿美元并挽救 11.4 万条生命
articles.author: karakoram

zh.thesis: 全民医保不仅能省钱，还能每年挽救超过十万条生命，问题只在于钱怎么分配。
paragraphs: 耶鲁大学牵头的一项预印本研究模拟发现，如果美国推行类似「全民医保法案」的国家公共保险计划，每年能省下 1.04 万亿美元医疗开支，还能多保住 11.4 万条命。
节省主要来自五个渠道：药品降价、支付标准向 Medicare 看齐、行政开销减少、欺诈账单减少，以及可避免的急诊和住院减少。即便按保守估计，每年也能省 6630 亿美元。
死亡人数的减少也来自覆盖的扩大：全面覆盖每年可避免约 6.3 万人死亡，其中近一半、约 3 万人是有保险但保险不足的人——超过 4500 万劳动年龄人口因免赔额和自付费用而仍然看不起病。
研究者承认有局限：过渡成本、行政裁员、提供方可能的反应都没算进去。但他们认为，美国花在医疗上的钱已经够多了，问题只是分配方式——覆盖所有人不需要新发现，只需要立法。

en.thesis: Universal health coverage would save both money and more than 100,000 lives a year; the problem is allocation, not funding.
paragraphs: A preprint study led by Yale researchers models what would happen if the US adopted a national public insurance plan like the one in the Medicare for All Act. It finds annual savings of $1.04 trillion in health spending and more than 114,000 lives saved.

Savings come from five sources: lower drug prices, Medicare-level payment rates, less administrative overhead, less fraudulent billing, and fewer avoidable ER visits and hospitalizations. Even on conservative assumptions the savings reach $663 billion a year.

On deaths, full coverage would avert about 62,863 annually, and nearly half of those — 29,631 — would be among people who already carry insurance. These are the underinsured: over 45 million working-age adults whose deductibles and cost-sharing still put care out of reach.

The authors concede limits: transition costs, job losses in administration, and how providers might react are not in the model. But they argue the US already spends enough — covering everyone needs no new discovery, only enactment.

articles.title: The Ellisons Again Threaten To Move CBS/Paramount Somewhere Shittier And Hotter If State Antitrust Lawsuit Isn’t Settled
articles.titleZh: 埃里森家族再次威胁：若州反垄断诉讼不和解，就把 CBS/派拉蒙搬去更差更热的地方
articles.author: Karl Bode

zh.thesis: 埃里森家族威胁搬走公司，但这只是虚张声势，因为加州总检察长并不买账，而且无论交易是否获批，生产外流都可能发生。
paragraphs: 拉里和戴维·埃里森正因 12 个州的反垄断诉讼而焦头烂额，该诉讼可能破坏他们 1110 亿美元的媒体帝国梦。近一两个月，他们显得越来越绝望。
据 Puck 报道，戴维·埃里森正筹划若加州总检察长罗伯·邦塔不和解，就将派拉蒙迁往田纳西、得克萨斯、乔治亚等州。但这威胁似乎没用，邦塔指责他们「敲诈」。
关键是，制作外流本就在发生，无论交易是否获批。而且员工反而松了口气，因为合并暂停让他们能专注工作。时间站在邦塔一边，因为从 10 月起，埃里森每天要付 700 万美元的拖延费。
所以对监管者来说，最好的策略就是直接阻止这类合并。历史数据表明，合并总导致大规模裁员、涨价和竞争力下降。埃里森可能两头输：要么交易被否，要么背上巨额债务，眼睁睁看着传统电视走向消亡。

en.thesis: The Ellisons' threat to move the company is bluster, since the California AG isn't buying it, and production flight may happen anyway.
paragraphs: Larry and David Ellison are rattled by a 12-state antitrust lawsuit that could sink their $111 billion media empire. The last month or two has shown growing desperation.

Per Puck, David Ellison is laying groundwork to move Paramount to Tennessee, Texas, Georgia, or elsewhere if California AG Rob Bonta doesn't settle. But the threat seems hollow — Bonta calls it 'blackmail'.

The key point is that production flight was already happening, with or without the deal. Employees are actually relieved the merger is paused, letting them focus on work. Time is on Bonta's side, as the Ellisons face a $7 million daily ticking fee from October.

So the best move for regulators is to block such mergers outright. History shows they lead to layoffs, higher prices, and less competition. Ellison may lose either way: the deal gets blocked, or he wins and drowns in debt while broadcast TV fades.

articles.title: Google has acquired the data of failed US airline Spirit
articles.titleZh: 谷歌拍下已破产的美国航空公司 Spirit 的数据
articles.author: pseudolus

zh.thesis: 谷歌花一千万美元买下 Spirit 航空的海量数据，意在训练 AI 模型。
paragraphs: Spirit 航空在 2020 年疫情中遭遇财务危机，之后一直没能恢复，2026 年 5 月停飞并进入清算。现在公司正在拍卖资产抵债。
上周的法院文件显示，谷歌以 1000 万美元拍下了一大批脱敏数据：1 亿封邮件、500 万条 Teams 消息、1700 万个 OneDrive 文件，还有 3000 多万通客服录音。
此外还包括 60 万张服务工单、1370 万个活跃邮箱地址，以及 76.3 万个航班的运营数据。谷歌表示买下这些数据是为了改进 AI 服务。
数据已经脱敏，谷歌也承诺会清除任何个人隐私信息。但《The Register》认为，未来某些 AI 提示词仍然可能意外泄露个人信息。

en.thesis: Google spent $10 million on bankrupt Spirit Airlines' data, with an eye to training AI models.
paragraphs: Spirit Airlines ran into financial trouble when COVID-19 hit in 2020, never recovered, and grounded itself permanently in May 2026. It is now liquidating, auctioning off assets to settle debts.

A court filing last week shows Google won a bid for a massive trove of deidentified data for just $10 million: 100 million emails, 5 million Teams messages, 17 million OneDrive files, and over 30 million recorded customer service calls.
The collection also includes 600,000 service tickets, 13.7 million active email addresses, and operational data from 763,000 flights. Google said it bought the data to improve its AI services.

The data has been deidentified and Google promised to scrub any personal information it finds. Still, The Register suspects that some personal info will inevitably surface in future prompts or searches.

articles.title: Teaching Everyone to Fish for Tokens
articles.author: Nathan Lambert

zh.thesis: 开源模型的未来取决于英伟达能否靠开放训练配方获利，否则开源将退居长尾。
paragraphs: 拿开源模型和 Linux 相比，其实要看怎么比。开放权重模型就像软件的一个版本，比如很多公司还在跑 Llama 3。而像 Olmo 那样连数据、代码带训练配方全开放的，才是真正意义上开源的系统。
英伟达大力投资接近开源的模型，比如 Nemotron，就是想让人人都能造出产 Token 的机器。这样一来，智能就不会被垄断，但推理需求会暴涨，大家都得来买它的芯片。
不过这条路能不能走通，要看经济账。现在英伟达投了 260 亿美元来养开源生态，但训练越来越贵，退出训练的公司像 Databricks 和 01.ai 还是少数。更麻烦的是，如今大家更爱微调现成的模型，而不是从零训练。
如果未来几年英伟达的回报远低于投入，或者没有下一家开源企业能建立起平台式的收益闭环，开源模型就会走上另一条路：重效率、可修改、专精化，去填闭源模型看不上的长尾场景，比如企业内部的私有数据代理。
Meta 也在做类似的事，但它和英伟达策略不同。Meta 放出很强的开源权重模型，纯粹是为了打压靠卖 Token 盈利的 OpenAI 和 Anthropic，这属于用战略放水来搞垮对手。

en.thesis: The future of open models hinges on whether Nvidia can profit from open training recipes; otherwise open source will retreat to a long tail.
paragraphs: Comparing open models to Linux depends on what you measure. Open-weight models are like a specific software version, which is why many companies still run workflows built on Llama 3. Models like Olmo, which ship data, code, and the full recipe, are the real open-source systems.

Nvidia is investing heavily in nearly open models like Nemotron because it wants everyone to be able to build token machines. That spreads intelligence around, but it also drives inference demand, and everyone who wants to run those machines needs to buy its chips.

The economics are still unproven. Nvidia is spending $26 billion to support the open ecosystem, but training costs are rising, and the companies dropping out, like Databricks and 01.ai, are still the exception. Meanwhile the fashion has shifted from training your own model to fine-tuning existing ones.

If the numbers don't work in a few years, or if no other open lab builds a platform-like revenue loop, open models will fork toward efficiency, modifiability, and specialization. They would fill the long tail closed models ignore, like on-prem enterprise agents running on private data.

Meta is doing something similar but with a different motive. Releasing a strong open-weight model like Muse Spark 1.2 is a strategic flood of tokens, meant to undercut the token-selling business of OpenAI and Anthropic rather than to build a self-sustaining ecosystem.

articles.title: Why Aren’t Modernist Bridges Awful?
articles.titleZh: 为什么现代主义桥梁不丑？
articles.author: Alex Tabarrok

zh.thesis: 现代桥梁之所以比现代建筑更受欢迎，是因为它们由工程师设计，而非建筑师。
paragraphs: 公众普遍讨厌现代建筑，却很少讨厌现代桥梁。全球最美桥梁榜单上，既有伦敦塔桥、布鲁克林桥等经典，也有巴西的库比契克桥、希腊的里翁-安蒂里翁大桥。
这背后有个理论：桥梁设计师来自工程学院，而非建筑学院。可能桥梁的工程约束自然带来美感，但丑桥也存在，所以并非纯属约束。
一个佐证是：建筑杂志《Wallpaper》选出的最美桥梁大多很丑，与大众喜欢的不重叠。这说明丑陋是选择，而非必然，正如塞缪尔·休斯所说。

en.thesis: Modern bridges are better received than modern buildings because they come from engineers, not architects.
paragraphs: The public broadly dislikes modern architecture, but it does not generally dislike modern bridges. Lists of the world's most beautiful bridges include classics like London's Tower Bridge and the Brooklyn Bridge, but also Brazil's Kubitschek Bridge and Greece's Rio-Antirrio Bridge.

A theory: bridge designers come from engineering schools rather than schools of architecture. Maybe the engineering constraints naturally lead to beauty, but ugly bridges do exist, so it is not just constraint.

One telling piece of evidence: Wallpaper, an architecture magazine, picks bridges that are mostly ugly, with no overlap with the popular ones. That suggests ugliness is a choice, not a necessity, as Samuel Hughes argues.

articles.title: Where to eat in San Francisco
articles.author: Noah Smith

zh.thesis: 旧金山的餐饮并不差，只是贵且分布不均，而且关键在于你会不会点。
paragraphs: 经济学博主给美食建议是有传统的，Tyler Cowen 甚至写过一本关于怎么吃的书。我也吃了旧金山几百家餐厅，差不多可以写一份像样的指南了。
很多人说旧金山是美食沙漠，我不信。这主要是技术问题：纽约和洛杉矶确实更好，但那是因为城市大得多，好餐厅的数量自然也多。
旧金山真正的毛病是房租太贵，加上开餐厅的繁琐手续，导致两头大中间小：要么是人均 600 美元的高级餐厅，要么是几美元的便宜货，中间价位很难找。
还有一个常被忽略的因素：旧金山的地铁不给力，又是山城，大家基本只在自己社区活动，餐厅之间竞争不充分，也就没动力创新。
尽管如此，我还是发现了三类旧金山做得特别好的餐厅：伪居酒屋、新派 fine dining，以及新开的苍蝇馆子。伪居酒屋用日式小盘分享的模式做各国菜，人均 70 到 110 美元，性价比很高。
新派 fine dining 人均只要 90 到 120 美元，就能吃到接近米其林水准的体验，比如 Mijoté 只要 84 美元。苍蝇馆子里藏着全城最好的四川菜、饺子、越南三明治和尼泊尔菜。
我的推荐标准是「每美元的美味」，所以人均 6 美元的越南三明治和 84 美元的套餐同样值得上榜。我写的只是我的主观感受，口味因人而异，别全信。
如果你想在旧金山好好吃一顿，去 Mission 区就对了，那里是真正的美食中心；像 SoMa 这种地方就避开吧，那儿简直是美食荒漠。

en.thesis: San Francisco's food scene is not bad, just expensive and unevenly distributed, and it's all about knowing where to look.
paragraphs: Economists recommending restaurants is a tradition; Tyler Cowen wrote a whole book on how to eat. I've tried a few hundred places in SF, so I can write a decent guide.
People call SF a food desert, and I don't buy it. It's a skill issue: NYC and LA are better, sure, but that's because they're much bigger cities, so they have more good restaurants by sheer numbers.
SF's real problems are insane rents and red tape, which produce a double-peaked distribution: either $600-a-person fine dining or cheap eats, with very little in between.
Another overlooked factor is mobility: SF's transit is weak, so people stick to their neighborhoods, restaurants don't compete, and there's little incentive to innovate.

That said, I've found three types SF does particularly well: pseudo-izakayas, hipster fine dining, and new hole-in-the-walls. Pseudo-izakayas use small plates and cross-cultural ingredients, usually $70–110 a head, and offer great variety.
Hipster fine dining gives you a near-Michelin experience for $90–120, like Mijoté at just $84. And the hole-in-the-walls hide the city's best Sichuan, dumplings, banh mi, and Nepalese food.
My ranking criterion is that units are 'yums per dollar,' so a $6 banh mi and an $84 tasting menu can both be top picks. This is all subjective, so take it with a grain of salt.
If you want a great meal in SF, head to the Mission — it's the real food hub. Avoid SoMa; it's a bona fide food desert.

articles.title: How economics is changing
articles.titleZh: 经济学正在发生怎样的变化
articles.author: Tyler Cowen

zh.thesis: 经济学研究越来越重视因果推断，这反映了学科重心的转移。
paragraphs: 经济学研究的重心正在偏移。计量理论、货币政策、公司治理的论文占比在下降，而发展经济学、犯罪、性别这些领域则在上升。
背后的原因可能是学者兴趣变了，也可能是需求端的压力——政策制定者的优先级和外部资金流向。
更重要的是，因果推断变得流行。1990 年文献中只有 7.7% 的主张是因果性的，2023 年这个数字涨到了 32.6%。而且，因果性越强的论文更容易被引用，也更容易进顶级期刊。

en.thesis: Economics research is increasingly focused on causal inference, reflecting a shift in the discipline's center of gravity.
paragraphs: The center of gravity in economics is shifting. Papers on econometric theory, monetary policy, and corporate governance have slumped as a share of the literature, while development, crime, and gender are on the rise.
The reasons could be changing intellectual interests or demand-side pressures—policy priorities and the direction of external funding.

More striking is the rise of causal claims. In 1990 only 7.7% of claims in the literature were causal; by 2023 that had hit 32.6%. And papers with more causal claims are more likely to be cited and to land in the top journals.

articles.title: 🎙️ How I AI: How a solo founder used Codex and ChatGPT to launch a fashion brand without engineers
articles.titleZh: 一个没有工程师的创始人，如何用 AI 做时装品牌
articles.author: Lenny Rachitsky

zh.thesis: AI 能让一个人在没有工程师的情况下，完成从设计到上线的整个时装品牌。
paragraphs: Yana Welinder 独自创立了时装品牌 Yana Bana，没有工程师团队。她靠 ChatGPT 和 Codex，把手绘草图变成逼真的产品图，操作专业 3D 时装软件，还能自己搭建带投票和支付功能的电商网站。
她的关键做法是把提示词当规格说明。生成图片前，她会详细描述轮廓、面料的垂坠感和声音。像这样的前期工作，能大幅提升结果质量。
AI 让她无需多年训练就能用上专业工具。她没学过 CLO，但用 Codex 操作它生成了 3D 打印所需的 CAD 文件。以后，人们可能不用再精通每个复杂软件，就能做出专业作品。
未来，AI 是编排层，专业软件负责执行。Codex 自己生成不了 CAD 文件，但操作 CLO 就能做到。这种模式让许多以前不划算的想法变得可行，瓶颈常在于那些繁琐的准备工作。

en.thesis: AI lets one person launch a fashion brand — from design to e-commerce — without engineers.
paragraphs: Yana Welinder runs the fashion brand Yana Bana alone, with no engineering team. With ChatGPT and Codex she turns hand sketches into realistic product shots, drives professional 3D fashion software, and builds an e-commerce site with voting and payments herself.

Her key move is treating the prompt as the spec. Before generating an image she describes the silhouette, how the fabric should drape, even the sound it makes. That upfront work sharply improves results.

AI lets her use expert tools she never learned. She drives CLO, a 3D fashion design app, through Codex, and gets the CAD files she needs for 3D printing. Soon people may not need to master every complex tool to produce professional work.

The near future is AI as the orchestration layer over purpose-built software. Codex cannot output a finished CAD file alone, but driving CLO it does exactly what she needs. This pattern is unlocking ideas that used to be impractical, because the bottleneck was the tedious prep work.
